pine-vellum.$description: Pine Vellum — Page canvas, all section backgrounds, box-shadow tint for the only subtle elevation present

cedar-stroke.$description: Cedar Stroke — Stroke color for background architectural illustrations, icon outlines, sage decorative line art, secondary borders

parchment.$description: Parchment — Primary text, link text, outlined button borders, heading characters, and the full suite of hairline rules and dividers

aged-tan.$description: Aged Tan — Muted secondary text and metadata labels (project years, category tags) — sits between parchment and the background, a quieter tertiary

editorialold.$description: Primary editorial serif — runs the entire information layer: navigation links, project titles, body paragraphs, list items, inline labels. Weight 200 across all sizes keeps the type from competing with the architectural background; this is the workhorse face and everything else is a special occasion. Letter-spacing stays at +0.004–0.005em, giving the thin strokes a touch of air without becoming formal.

wispy.$description: The single monumental display cut — used exactly once for the owner's name in the hero. The -0.01em tracking pulls the hairlines tight; this is the only place the design allows itself to be loud, and it earns that volume by being the only 96px element on the page.

old-standard-tt.$description: Google-available fallback for EditorialOld at the smallest sizes — 13px captions and 16px secondary paragraphs. Same ultra-light weight, same manuscript register.

gta.$description: A secondary body serif with slightly more open leading (1.60) and a touch more weight (300) — appears in longer-form sections where the tighter EditorialOld would feel constraining. Looser tracking at +0.004em matches the primary family.

bodoni-classic-ornaments.$description: Ornamental display face — used sparingly for the small decorative motifs embedded in body text (flourishes, dingbats, the small flowers in the rose-window pattern). Wider tracking (+0.011em) is intentional, these characters need room to breathe as mark-making rather than text.

altesse-std-24pt.$description: Reserved display serif for mid-level section headers — the rare heading that isn't set in EditorialOld. Tight line-height (1.10) and the highest stroke contrast in the family make it feel like a pull-quote.

ui-sans-serif.$description: System fallback for the rare non-serif surface — the keyboard-shortcut chips (W, T, A) in the navigation, where a monospaced feel is needed for the boxed letter.
